subject.title: [Bug]: IRC channel reports healthy while dead-looping reconnects on a non-recoverable login error

question: For IRC post-ready reconnects that hit fatal login codes 432, 464, or 465, should OpenClaw mark the account terminally disconnected or keep retrying with capped backoff while reporting connected:false and lastError?
rationale: The source bug is clear, but the permanent-stop versus retry-after-operator-fix behavior is an operator policy choice that code should not guess.

options.title: Capped retry with honest status
options.body: Report connected:false and lastError immediately, retry with bounded backoff, and let operators repair server-side credentials or bans without restarting OpenClaw.

options.title: Terminal fatal disconnect
options.body: Treat 432, 464, and 465 after reconnect as terminal, stop the IRC monitor, and require explicit operator restart after fixing configuration or server-side state.

options.title: Defer to shared channel policy
options.body: Pause the IRC-specific fix until maintainers decide a common fatal transport policy for all channel plugins.

recommendation.title: Capped retry with honest status
recommendation.body: Report connected:false and lastError immediately, retry with bounded backoff, and let operators repair server-side credentials or bans without restarting OpenClaw.

likelyOwner.reason: They validated and landed the adjacent IRC reconnect behavior, so they are the best available routing owner for the policy choice.
